items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: Let me put in a plug for her. Her name is Emma Franz

ctx.x: Let’s talk about the logistics, the reality. Because earlier today we were talking about someone who wanted to make a film about Bill Frisell, and I remember I forget now, I wanted to write it down.

Let me put in a plug for her. Her name is Emma Franz, it’s F-R-A-N-Z, and she’s a jazz singer out of Australia, but she did this incredible film called “Intangible Assets Number 82” about an Australian drummer, Simon Baker, who was captivated by the sound of a Korean shaman. Shamans use drums to go into a trance. It was a shamanic drummer who is legendary. And he did many pilgrimages to try to see him and none of them ever quite worked. And she managed to go on one trip with a great crew, it’s a beautifully shot…
And you said, I can’t remember the words, but you were referring to finding funding, like a hard nut.
